Lehsuni Dhaniya Paneer (Garlic Coriander Paneer)

Transcribed from reel caption

Garlic-coriander paneer: a fried paneer block simmered in a yogurt-and-cream gravy with mustard oil, onion and a handful of fresh coriander. High-protein (22g per serving, 390 kcal), serves 2.

Paneer & Main

  • 200g low-fat paneer (whole block)
  • 2 tbsp mustard oil
  • 2 onions, finely chopped
  • 1 tsp chilli garlic paste
  • 3 tbsp yogurt
  • 100ml water
  • 1 tsp brown sugar
  • 2 tbsp fresh cream
  • Fresh coriander, to garnish

Spices & Aromatics

  • 1 handful fresh coriander, chopped
  • 1 green chilli, chopped
  • 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
  • 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder
  • 1 1/4 tsp coriander powder
  • 1 tsp salt

Steps

  1. Heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the whole 200g paneer block and fry until golden brown on both sides, then set aside.
  2. Chop the fried paneer into cubes.
  3. In the same oil, saute the 2 finely chopped onions until golden brown.
  4. Add 1 tsp chilli garlic paste and saute for 2 minutes.
  5. Add the handful of chopped fresh coriander, the chopped green chilli, turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Mix really well until the spices are nicely combined.
  6. Add 3 tbsp yogurt and 100ml water; stir well.
  7. Add the fried paneer cubes back into the pan. Sprinkle in 1 tsp brown sugar and add 2 tbsp fresh cream.
  8. Mix everything well and let it simmer until the gravy thickens and coats the paneer beautifully.
  9. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve.

Creamy One-Pot Mushroom Chicken

Transcribed from reel caption (ingredients only; full method sent by creator on comment)

A creamy one-pot mushroom chicken from a fall chicken series — 'feels fancy without actually doing the most.' The caption lists ingredients; steps below follow the one-pot order of the ingredient list.

Chicken & Seasoning

  • 1 lb chicken thighs
  • 2 tsp salt & black pepper
  • 2 tsp garlic powder
  • 2 tsp onion powder
  • 2 tsp smoked paprika

Sauce

  • 2 shallots, minced
  • 1 head garlic, minced
  • 8 oz portobello mushrooms, sliced
  • 2 tbsp flour
  • 1/2 cup white wine
  • 1 1/2 cups chicken broth
  • 1 cup heavy whipping cream
  • 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 tsp fresh thyme
  • 1 tsp fresh tarragon
  • 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese

Garnish

  • Parsley and/or fresh chives

Steps

  1. Season the chicken thighs with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and smoked paprika.
  2. Brown the chicken in a hot pot; remove and set aside.
  3. Saute the shallots, minced garlic and sliced portobello mushrooms; stir in the flour to coat.
  4. Deglaze with the white wine, then add the chicken broth, heavy cream, Worcestershire sauce, thyme and tarragon.
  5. Return the chicken to the pot and simmer until cooked through and the sauce thickens.
  6. Stir in the Parmesan, garnish with parsley or chives, and serve.

Chicken Barra

Transcribed from reel

A rich, velvety, restaurant-style chicken dish made at home.

Marination

  • 2 lbs boneless chicken
  • 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
  • 3 tbsp fried onion paste
  • 1 tbsp green chili paste
  • 1/2 cup yogurt
  • 1.5 tbsp lemon juice
  • 1 tbsp oil
  • Orange food color

Spices

  • Salt to taste
  • 1.5 tsp red chili
  • 1/2 tsp turmeric
  • 1.5 tsp coriander powder
  • 1 tsp garam masala
  • 1 tsp cumin powder
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • 1 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek)

Gravy & Finish

  • 2-3 tbsp oil/butter
  • 1/2 cup fresh cream
  • 1/4 cup water
  • 1/2 red onion, cut into petals
  • 1/4 cup cilantro

Steps

  1. Marinate: coat the chicken in the ginger-garlic paste, fried onion paste, green chili paste, yogurt, lemon juice, oil, food color, and all the spices.
  2. Fry: cook the chicken in oil over medium-high heat until charred and cooked through. Set aside. (Optional: smoke with charcoal before or after frying for a traditional touch.)
  3. Gravy: in the same pan, simmer the remaining marinade with water until the oil separates. Stir in the fresh cream and 1 tsp sugar (optional) on low heat until smooth.
  4. Toss: add the chicken, onion petals, and cilantro. Fold together for 1-2 minutes and enjoy!

Big Chocolate Chip Cookies for Two

https://sugaredandstirred.com/big-chocolate-chip-cookies-for-two/

Two big chocolate chunk cookies. Small-batch, no-chill, with pools of melty chocolate and a sprinkling of sea salt.

Cookie Dough

  • Softened butter
  • Sugar
  • 1 egg yolk
  • All-purpose flour
  • Large dark chocolate chunks
  • Flaky sea salt, for sprinkling

Steps

  1. Mix the softened butter with the sugar and the egg yolk in a glass bowl until combined.
  2. Fold in the flour with a spatula, then fold in the large dark chocolate chunks.
  3. Scoop the dough into two large balls and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
  4. Bake until the cookies have spread with golden, crisp edges and soft centers.
  5. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt while warm. Pull apart and enjoy the gooey interior.

Makes two big cookies. For full measurements, see the creator's recipe page linked above.

Chicken Queso Blanco

Ingredients from reel caption; steps transcribed from reel video

A simple, crowd-pleasing chicken queso blanco dip - great for game days.

Chicken

  • 1 lb chicken breast
  • 1 tsp chili powder
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • 2 tsp salt
  • 2 tsp black pepper
  • 2 tsp onion powder
  • 2 tsp garlic powder
  • 2 tbsp olive oil

Queso

  • 2 tbsp butter
  • 1/2 yellow onion, diced
  • 4 cloves garlic, grated
  • 3 cups milk
  • 1 lb white American cheese, sliced
  • 8 oz Monterey Jack cheese, shredded
  • 4 oz green chiles, diced

Toppings

  • 3 Roma tomatoes, diced
  • 1 tbsp cilantro, chopped

Steps

  1. Drizzle the chicken breasts with olive oil and season with the chili powder, smoked paprika, salt, black pepper, onion powder, and garlic powder.
  2. Sear the chicken in a pan until browned and cooked through; remove from the pan.
  3. In the same pan, melt the butter and saute the diced onion, then add the grated garlic.
  4. Pour in the milk and add the white American cheese slices and shredded Monterey Jack. Whisk until smooth and creamy.
  5. Pulse the cooked chicken in a food processor until finely chopped, then return it to the sauce along with the diced green chiles.
  6. Stir everything together and season with salt and pepper.
  7. Transfer to a serving pan and top with the diced tomatoes and chopped cilantro. Serve warm with tortilla chips.

One-Pan Roast Chicken with Herby Garlic Butter

Steps transcribed from reel video

An easy, nutritious one-pan roast chicken dinner with roasted vegetables and a creamy herby garlic butter sauce.

Chicken & Vegetables

  • 1 whole chicken
  • Potatoes, chopped
  • Carrots, chopped
  • 1 onion, sliced
  • Lemon halves
  • Fresh rosemary sprigs
  • Salt and pepper, to season

Herby Garlic Butter & Sauce

  • Softened butter
  • Fresh rosemary, stripped and minced
  • Fresh parsley, minced
  • Garlic, minced
  • A thick, creamy sauce, to pour over the finished dish

Steps

  1. Chop the carrots, halve the lemons, and strip and mince the fresh rosemary and parsley; mince the garlic.
  2. Mix the herbs and garlic into the softened butter to make the herby garlic butter.
  3. Place the chopped potatoes, carrots, and sliced onions in a black cast iron skillet; season and top with the lemon halves and rosemary sprigs.
  4. Place the whole raw chicken on top of the vegetables and rub the herby garlic butter under and over the skin.
  5. Roast until the chicken is golden-brown and cooked through.
  6. Carve the chicken on a board and arrange it back in the skillet with the roasted vegetables.
  7. Serve onto plates and pour the melted creamy sauce generously over the chicken and vegetables.

Exact quantities were not given in the reel; season and portion to taste.

Paneer Kaju Masala (No Onion, No Garlic)

Transcribed from reel video

No onion, no garlic, ready in 35 minutes - and absolutely paisa vasool.

Paneer & Puree

  • Paneer, cut into triangular shapes
  • Tomatoes
  • Cashew nuts
  • Yogurt
  • Green chilies
  • Oil, for frying

Gravy

  • Ghee
  • Whole spices: cumin, star anise, cinnamon
  • Kashmiri red chili powder
  • Water
  • Fresh cream
  • Cilantro, chopped
  • Whole cashews and almonds, to garnish

Steps

  1. Cut the paneer into geometric triangular shapes and lightly fry until golden brown; set aside.
  2. Blend the tomatoes, cashew nuts, yogurt, and green chilies into a smooth orange puree.
  3. Heat ghee in a pan and add the whole spices (cumin, star anise, cinnamon), then the Kashmiri red chili powder.
  4. Pour in the blended puree and cook it down.
  5. Add the fried paneer and some water, cover, and let it cook.
  6. Finish with a swirl of cream and chopped cilantro.
  7. Plate in a bowl, garnish with whole cashews, almonds, and fresh cilantro, and serve with roti.

Creamy Tomato Pasta Soup with Chicken

Transcribed from reel

A family-favorite soup - creamy, comforting, and easy.

Soup

  • 5 cloves garlic, diced
  • 1 tsp chili flakes
  • 1/2 onion, diced
  • 1 celery stick, diced
  • 1/2 carrot, diced
  • 1 cup crushed tomato
  • 1 spoon sugar
  • 2 tsp basil
  • 4 tsp oregano
  • 4 cups water
  • 2 cups milk
  • Pasta of choice
  • 1/2 chicken breast, diced
  • Cheese, to top
  • Salt and pepper, to taste

Steps

  1. In a pan, add the diced garlic, chili flakes, and diced onion; saute for two minutes.
  2. Add the diced celery and carrot and cook until the veggies are halfway done.
  3. Add the crushed tomato and saute for another 2 to 3 minutes.
  4. Add the sugar, basil, and oregano.
  5. Add the water and milk with the pasta of choice and bring to a boil.
  6. Add the diced chicken breast and boil for another 5 to 7 minutes.
  7. Top with cheese, season with salt and pepper to taste, and serve.

Cheesy Garlic Knots

Transcribed from reel (full recipe on elizabethsrecipediary.com)

Soft, fluffy knots stuffed with mozzarella and brushed with garlic-parmesan butter.

Dough

  • 1 1/3 cups warm water, about 110 F (320 g)
  • 2 1/4 tsp instant yeast (1 packet)
  • 1 tbsp sugar
  • 3 tbsp olive oil (40 g)
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  • 1/2 tsp oregano
  • 3 1/2 cups bread flour (420 g)
  • 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
  • 1 egg, beaten

Garlic butter topping

  • 1/2 cup salted butter, melted
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/4 cup parmesan cheese
  • 3 tbsp minced parsley

Steps

  1. Whisk the warm water, yeast and sugar; rest 5 minutes. Add the olive oil, salt, garlic powder, oregano and half the flour; mix, then add the remaining flour until a shaggy dough forms.
  2. Knead 5 minutes on a floured surface. Cover and rise in a warm place 1 hour, until doubled.
  3. Divide into 8 pieces and roll into logs. Flatten each log into a 1-inch-wide rectangle, line with shredded mozzarella, seal lengthwise, then double-knot each log, tucking the ends underneath. Space 2 inches apart on a baking sheet.
  4. Mix the garlic butter topping ingredients. Cover the knots and rise 30 minutes in a warm place.
  5. Brush with the beaten egg and garlic butter topping; bake at 400 F for 20 minutes. Brush with garlic butter again to finish.

Creamy Sausage Tortellini Soup

Transcribed from reel

A hug-in-a-bowl soup: two kinds of sausage, cheese tortellini, and spinach in a creamy tomato-Parmesan broth.

Soup

  • 1 tbsp oil
  • Sliced andouille sausage
  • Ground hot Italian sausage
  • 1 onion, diced
  • Salt and black pepper
  • 3-4 garlic cloves, minced
  • Chopped sun-dried tomatoes
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • Dried herbs (Italian seasoning)
  • 2 tbsp flour
  • 4-5 cups chicken broth
  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • 1/2 cup grated Parmesan
  • Fresh cheese tortellini
  • Fresh spinach, a large handful

Steps

  1. Heat oil and sear the sliced andouille until browned; set aside. Brown the ground hot Italian sausage; remove and set aside.
  2. Saute the diced onion with salt and pepper, then add garlic and sun-dried tomatoes. Stir in the tomato paste and dried herbs.
  3. Sprinkle over the flour and stir, then pour in the chicken broth.
  4. Return both sausages to the pot. Stir in the heavy cream and Parmesan.
  5. Add the tortellini and chopped spinach; simmer until the tortellini is tender and the spinach has wilted.
  6. Ladle into bowls and serve garnished with extra Parmesan.

Crispy fried potato balls with a molten mozzarella center, tossed in garlic butter — made for a pregnancy craving.

Jalapeno Cheddar Upside Down Cornbread

Transcribed from reel (recipe by @bakedwithlovebyivy)

Cornbread baked upside down over caramel and jalapeno coins, so the top comes out sweet, spicy, and glossy.

Cornbread

  • 1 cup cornmeal
  • 1 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 tsp baking soda
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • 1/4 tsp salt
  • 4 tbsp butter, melted
  • 1/4 cup olive oil
  • 1/3 cup brown or coconut sugar
  • 2 tbsp honey
  • 1 egg
  • 1 cup buttermilk
  • 1/4 cup cheddar, small dice

Caramel jalapeno layer

  • 2 jalapenos, sliced into thin coins
  • 3/4 cup white sugar
  • 1/4 cup water

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 350 F. Whisk together the cornmeal, flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt.
  2. In another bowl, whisk the melted butter, oil, brown sugar, honey, egg, and buttermilk; fold into the dry mix until just combined, then fold in the cheddar.
  3. Grease an 8x8 pan or 8-9 inch cast-iron skillet and line with parchment. Arrange the jalapeno coins in concentric circles across the bottom.
  4. In a saucepan, swirl the sugar and water over medium heat (do not stir) until a medium amber caramel forms. Pour the hot caramel over the jalapenos.
  5. Top with the cornbread batter. Bake 20-22 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
  6. Cool no more than 5 minutes, run a knife around the edges, and invert onto a serving plate. Slice and enjoy.

Crispy Smashed Potatoes with Kewpie-Ponzu Sauce

Transcribed from reel

Crisp-edged smashed potatoes tossed in a garlicky Kewpie-ponzu-style sauce with lemon and fresh herbs — a family favorite.

Potatoes

Kewpie-ponzu sauce

Kathy's Lasagna

Transcribed from reel

A big, classic meat lasagna made in honor of Kathy — sausage, beef, three cheeses, and no-boil noodles in three hearty layers.

Meat sauce

  • 1 lb Italian sausage
  • 1 lb lean ground beef
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1/2 cup yellow onion, diced
  • 4 garlic cloves, minced
  • 14 oz can diced tomatoes
  • 48 oz marinara sauce
  • 6 oz tomato paste
  • 1/2 cup water
  • 1/4 cup fresh parsley, finely chopped
  • 2 tsp dried basil
  • 2 tsp dried oregano
  • Salt, to taste

Cheese and assembly

  • 1 lb ricotta
  • 1 egg
  • 1 lb low-moisture mozzarella, grated
  • 1/2 cup Parmesan, grated
  • 1 package no-boil lasagna noodles

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 375 F.
  2. Saute the onion and garlic in olive oil in a Dutch oven for a minute; add the sausage and beef and cook until well browned. Season with salt; stir in the parsley, basil, oregano, and tomato paste and cook about 3 minutes until the paste browns in spots.
  3. Deglaze with the water, scraping the pot; stir in the diced tomatoes and marinara and simmer on low while preparing the rest.
  4. Mix the ricotta with the egg and a few pinches of salt.
  5. Build in a 9x13 dish: sauce, a layer of noodles, a third of the remaining sauce, half the ricotta, a third of the mozzarella; repeat a second layer; finish with a third noodle layer, the rest of the sauce, the remaining mozzarella, and the Parmesan.
  6. Cover and bake 25 minutes; uncover and bake 25 more minutes until golden and bubbly.

Vanilla Cake with Chocolate Frosting

Transcribed from reel

Classic birthday cake: vanilla layers with chocolate frosting (espresso powder optional).

Cake

  • 3 cups AP flour
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • Pinch of salt
  • 1 cup butter, room temp
  • 2 cups sugar
  • 4 large eggs
  • 1 cup buttermilk, room temp
  • 2 1/2 tsp vanilla

Frosting

  • 1 1/2 cups butter, softened
  • 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 5 cups powdered sugar
  • 1/2 cup heavy cream
  • 2 tsp vanilla
  • 1/2 tsp espresso powder (optional)

Steps

  1. Preheat to 350F. Prepare three 8 or 9 inch cake pans.
  2. Whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Set aside.
  3. Cream the butter, then add the sugar; cream together for about 8 minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing until just combined.
  4. Add one-third of the flour mixture and mix until combined; add half the buttermilk and mix. Repeat with another third of flour followed by the remaining buttermilk, ending with the last of the flour mixture, mixing each addition until combined. Mix in the vanilla.
  5. Divide the batter among the cake pans and bake 25-30 minutes, until the edges pull away from the pans and a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean.
  6. For the frosting: whisk the cocoa powder through to remove lumps. Cream together the butter and cocoa until well combined.
  7. Whisk the powdered sugar to remove lumps (or sift). Add the sugar and cream to the cocoa mixture — one cup of sugar followed by about a tablespoon of cream — turning the mixer to high for about 1 minute after each addition, until all is added. Add the vanilla (and espresso powder, if using) and combine well.
  8. Cool the cake layers about 10 minutes in the pans, then turn out onto wire racks and cool completely.
  9. Frost and enjoy.

Taylor Swift Chai Cookies

Source: https://myradkitchen.com/taylor-swift-chai-cookies/

Soft, sweet and spiced just right — chai sugar cookies with an eggnog glaze.

Cookies

  • 250 g all-purpose flour (about 2 cups)
  • 2 bags chai tea, cut open, leaves removed
  • 1/2 tsp baking soda
  • 1/4 tsp sea salt
  • 1 stick unsalted butter, room temperature
  • 1/2 cup vegetable oil
  • 100 g granulated sugar (about 1/2 cup), plus more for sprinkling
  • 60 g icing sugar (about 1/2 cup)
  • 1 large egg, room temperature
  • 2 tsp pure vanilla extract

Glaze

  • 180 g icing sugar (1 1/2 cups), sifted
  • 2 tbsp eggnog (or as needed)
  • 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon

Steps

  1. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, chai tea leaves, baking soda and salt; set aside.
  2. In a stand mixer, beat the butter on medium-low for 1 minute. Add the oil, granulated sugar and icing sugar and mix just until combined, with pieces of butter still intact.
  3. Add the egg and vanilla; mix 20-30 seconds to combine.
  4. Add the dry ingredients on low and mix to incorporate.
  5. Chill the dough in the fridge for 1 hour (longer chilling deepens the chai flavor).
  6. Preheat the oven to 350F; line a baking sheet with parchment.
  7. Drop 1 1/2-tablespoon portions of dough 2 inches apart. Press the tops down gently and sprinkle with sugar.
  8. Bake about 8 minutes, until the edges just start to turn golden. Cool on the pan 5-10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
  9. Whisk the icing sugar, eggnog, nutmeg and cinnamon into a glaze; spoon about 1 teaspoon onto the center of each cookie.
  10. Makes about 28 cookies.

Don't overbake — the cookies should look just barely golden around the edges. Any favorite chai brand works; if the spices are coarse, blitz them first.

Feuilletine (Crispy Wafer Flakes)

Source: https://thescranline.com/feuilletine-recipe/

Super thin, crispy wafer flakes that stay crisp even mixed into fat-based things like Nutella or ganache — a topping for brownies, cakes and cupcakes.

Feuilletine

  • 55 g salted butter, softened
  • 55 g powdered sugar, sifted
  • 1 large egg, room temperature
  • 7 g vanilla extract
  • 65 g all purpose flour
  • 1/4 tsp baking powder

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 165C/330F (155C/295F fan). Line two large baking trays with silicone mats.
  2. Whisk the softened butter and powdered sugar until combined; add the egg and vanilla and whisk in (it will look curdled).
  3. Mix in the flour and baking powder until a smooth paste forms.
  4. Divide between the two trays; spread as evenly and thinly as possible with an offset spatula or spoon.
  5. Bake each tray one at a time for 14-15 minutes, until a deep golden color — watch closely so it doesn't burn.
  6. Cool completely, then break into fairly large pieces.
  7. Store in an airtight container or zip lock bag; keeps 2 weeks (up to 3 days in the fridge per the source).

Use it mixed with frosting or Nutella, sprinkled over ice cream, folded into cake or cookie batter, or mixed into ganache — it stays crisp in fat-based mixtures.

Homemade Ice Cream Cake

Transcribed from reel

A few layers and a little freezer time — easier than it sounds, and endlessly customizable.

Oreo Crunch

  • 18 Oreo cookies
  • 3 tbsp butter, melted

Layers

  • 1.5 qt vanilla ice cream, slightly softened
  • 1 jar (11.75 oz) hot fudge sauce, warmed enough to spread
  • Cooled Oreo crumble
  • 1.5 qt cookies & cream ice cream, slightly softened

Frosting

  • 8 oz tub Cool Whip, thawed
  • 1 box (3.4 oz) instant vanilla pudding mix
  • 1 cup cold whole milk

Steps

  1. Make the Oreo crunch: pulse the Oreos in a food processor to gravel-sized clusters; toss with melted butter; spread on a parchment-lined baking sheet; bake at 350F for 8 minutes. Cool completely.
  2. Press the vanilla ice cream evenly into a 9-inch springform pan and smooth the top. Freeze 1 hour.
  3. Spread the warm hot fudge evenly over the ice cream. Sprinkle over the cooled Oreo crumble and press in gently. Freeze 2 hours.
  4. Add the cookies & cream ice cream and smooth the top. Freeze overnight (about 8 hours) until completely firm.
  5. For the frosting: mix the milk and pudding mix on high until incorporated; fold in the Cool Whip.
  6. Remove the cake from the springform pan (a quick pass of a hair dryer around the outside helps release it) and spread the frosting evenly over the cake. Freeze 1-2 hours.
  7. Let the cake sit at room temperature about 15 minutes before slicing.

Chocolate Fudge Frosting (No Mixer)

Full recipe on creator's website (bakewithzoha.com)

Unbelievably easy fudge frosting made in a saucepan with 4 basic ingredients — no chocolate, no mixer, and far less sweet than most frostings.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups (675g) unsalted butter
  • 1-1/3 cups (320g) whole milk
  • 3 cups (360g) powdered sugar
  • 1 cup (100g) cocoa powder, preferably Dutch-processed
  • 1 tsp instant coffee (optional, but recommended)
  • 1/2 tsp salt (optional, but recommended)

Steps

  1. Add all the ingredients to a large saucepan (or deep frying pan) over medium to medium-low heat.
  2. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the butter melts; it may look lumpy at first, but keep stirring and cooking until it turns into a smooth chocolatey sauce.
  3. Keep cooking and stirring until the mixture comes to a boil — it will bubble up, turn frothy all over and rise in volume, then start to thicken.
  4. After a few more minutes it will stop bubbling and become a thick, glossy chocolate sauce, about the consistency of thick chocolate syrup (10-15 minutes total cooking time).
  5. Pour into a wide dish such as a 9x13 pan and press cling wrap directly onto the surface so it doesn't form a skin.
  6. Refrigerate 1-2 hours, until firm and spreadable, then use on cakes or brownies.

Good cocoa powder is key since it does all the flavour work. Too firm or runny? Adjust by leaving it at room temperature or chilling longer. Keeps 5 days refrigerated in an airtight container.

Aloo Paratha (Foolproof Stuffing Trick)

Transcribed from reel

The trick to parathas that never burst: it's not just the spiced potato filling, it's the dough elasticity and how you seal the pockets.

  • Green chillies, chopped
  • Whole cumin, coriander and fennel seeds, roasted

Dough

  • Oil

Steps

  1. Knead a soft, elastic whole wheat dough and rest it well — elasticity is the key to parathas that don't tear.
  2. Mash the boiled potatoes and mix with salt, cumin, coriander, amchur and red chilli powders, plus cilantro, ginger and green chillies. Stir in the roasted whole spices.

  4. Roll out gently and evenly, keeping the filling sealed inside.

Curry

Garnish

Steps

  4. Add the curry powder, chilli flakes, soy sauce, salt, water, stock cube and condensed milk; simmer a couple of minutes.

S'mores Chocolate Chip Cookies

Transcribed from reel caption

Chocolate chip cookie dough stuffed with toasted marshmallow, chocolate and graham crackers — s'mores in cookie form.

Cookie dough

  • 1/2 cup (113 g) salted butter, melted
  • 1/3 cup (67 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) dark brown sugar
  • 1 tbsp (15 g) vanilla bean paste
  • 1/2 tsp espresso powder
  • 1 1/4 cups (156 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 tsp baking soda
  • 1 egg, at room temperature
  • 1 cup (170 g) semi-sweet chocolate chips

S'mores filling

  • 1/2 cup (85 g) mini chocolate rectangles (or chopped chocolate bar)
  • 8 large marshmallows
  • 8 graham cracker squares

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a bowl, whisk the melted butter with the granulated and brown sugars for 2–3 minutes until well combined. Crack in the egg and whisk 1–2 minutes until smooth, then whisk in the vanilla bean paste.
  3. In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking soda and espresso powder. Gradually fold the dry ingredients into the wet batter until just combined, then fold in the chocolate chips without overmixing.
  4. On the prepared baking sheet, lay out graham cracker squares. Top each with chocolate rectangles and a marshmallow. Scoop out a portion of cookie dough, flatten slightly, and place it over the marshmallow, covering it completely.
  5. Space the cookies 2–3 inches apart (3–4 per baking sheet) and bake 12–13 minutes, until the edges are golden and crisp and the centers are chewy and soft.
  6. Cool completely on the pan for 25–30 minutes before serving.

French Onion Gnocchi Soup

Transcribed from tasteofhome.com (linked by creator)

Classic French onion soup reimagined with tender potato gnocchi, finished under the broiler with melted Swiss/Gruyère and Parmesan.

Soup

  • 4 tbsp butter
  • 2 tbsp canola oil
  • 4 lb yellow onions, sliced 1/4-in. thin (about 6–7 medium)
  • 2 tsp packed brown sugar
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp pepper
  • 4 garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 3 tbsp all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup dry red wine or dry sherry
  • 6 cups beef stock
  • 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 3 sprigs fresh parsley
  • 2 fresh thyme sprigs
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 package (17-1/2 oz) potato gnocchi

Cheesy topping

  • 2 cups shredded Swiss or Gruyère cheese
  • 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
  • 2 tbsp minced fresh parsley, for garnish

Steps

  1. Heat the butter and oil in a Dutch oven or soup pot over medium-high heat. Stir in the onions, cover, and cook until softened, 10–15 minutes.
  2. Stir in the brown sugar, salt and pepper. Reduce the heat to medium-low and continue cooking, uncovered, until the onions reach a deep golden-brown color, 45–50 minutes.
  3. Add the garlic, tomato paste and flour; stir to distribute evenly and cook 2–3 minutes.
  4. Pour in the wine, scraping the bottom of the pot to release the browned bits. Add the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce and bring to a boil.
  5. Bundle the parsley, thyme and bay leaf together (cheesecloth or kitchen twine) and add to the pot. Reduce to a simmer and cook 45 minutes, then turn off the heat.
  6. Stir in the gnocchi and discard the herb bundle.
  7. Preheat the broiler. Ladle the soup into 6 oven-safe crocks or ramekins set on a sheet pan, filling about 3/4 full. Top each generously with Swiss/Gruyère and Parmesan.
  8. Broil 3–4 minutes until the cheese is melted and browned. Garnish with parsley and serve immediately.

Super Creamy Flan (4 Ingredients)

Transcribed from bakewithzoha.com (linked by creator)

An extra-silky leche flan made with only 4 main ingredients — a high yolk-to-egg ratio and heavy cream instead of evaporated milk, baked low and slow in a water bath. Make-ahead friendly: chill overnight.

Caramel

  • 1 cup granulated sugar (200 g)

Custard

  • 2 large eggs
  • 6 egg yolks
  • 1 can sweetened condensed milk (14 oz / 396 g)
  • 2 cups heavy cream (480 g)
  • 1 tsp vanilla bean paste (optional)
  • 1/2 tsp salt (optional)

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 300°F (conventional, no fan).
  2. For the caramel: spread the sugar evenly in a clean, dry, wide-bottomed stainless-steel pan over medium to medium-low heat. Let the bottom layer melt, then gently stir with a clean dry spatula so the top sugar melts too — lumps will melt down if you wait. Once all the sugar is melted and light golden, reduce to low and keep stirring gently until it reaches a deep golden-amber color; caramel burns quickly at this stage.
  3. Immediately pour the caramel into an 8-inch cake pan. Lift the pan with a towel (it gets hot fast) and tilt to coat the bottom and slightly up the sides. Refrigerate until the caramel hardens.
  4. For the custard: add the eggs and yolks to a bowl and whisk very gently — a slow stirring motion, not vigorous whisking — until broken down with no lumps and no air bubbles.
  5. Gently stir in the sweetened condensed milk, heavy cream, and vanilla and salt if using, until just combined.
  6. Strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into another bowl to remove eggy bits (strain gently, from a low height, to avoid adding air), then strain back into the original bowl.
  7. Strain the custard over the hardened caramel in the pan. Pop any surface bubbles — a hair dryer on the lowest setting held at a distance works.
  8. Set the flan pan inside a 9x13-inch pan and pour 1/2 inch of boiling water into the larger pan (avoiding the flan) to make a water bath.
  9. Bake 50–55 minutes, until the flan is set at the edges but still jiggles like jello in the middle when gently shaken; do not overbake.
  10. Lift the flan out of the water bath, rest 10 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate overnight or at least 4 hours.
  11. To unmold: run a knife around the edges, then set the pan on the stove over the lowest flame about 30 seconds, until the caramel loosens and the flan slips when shaken. Invert a serving plate over the pan, flip the two together, shake gently until the flan drops, and lift the pan away. Melt any leftover caramel in the pan and pour over the top. Slice and serve.

Chocolate Cake with Whipped Chocolate Ganache

Transcribed from reel

Dry Ingredients

  • 200g (1 cup) white granulated sugar
  • 120g (1 cup) all purpose flour
  • 35g (1/3 cup) cocoa powder
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • 1/2 tsp baking powder
  • 1/2 tsp coffee powder
  • 1 tsp salt

Wet Ingredients

  • 120g (1/2 cup) warm water
  • 120g (1/2 cup) buttermilk
  • 60g (1/4 cup) vegetable oil
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 tsp vanilla

Whipped Ganache

  • 270g (1 1/2 cups) dark chocolate chips / chopped compound chocolate bar
  • 135g (1/2 cup + 1 tbsp) heavy cream

Steps

  1. Preheat your oven to 300F (150C).
  2. In a bowl, sift and whisk the dry ingredients together.
  3. In a separate bowl whisk together all the wet ingredients until well combined.
  4. Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix gently until no streaks of flour remain. Do not overmix the batter.
  5. Grease 2 pcs of 6" round pan with a little oil and line the bottom with baking paper. Divide the batter into the pans (approximately 340g-350g of batter per pan).
  6. Tap the pans on the counter to release air bubbles. Then bake for 40-45 mins or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean. Cool completely before frosting.
  7. To make the ganache, heat the cream in the microwave or on the stove until it just starts to bubble. Then pour this over the chocolate. Mix thoroughly until all chocolate is dissolved. Cover and refrigerate. Once cold, beat the ganache using a whisk or a hand mixer until it doubles in volume and becomes lighter in color.
  8. Assemble the cake and enjoy.

Source caption notes you can also bake this in an 8x8 inch pan at the same temperature, but start checking for doneness at 30 minutes.

Thin Crispy Ripple Chocolate Chip Cookies

Transcribed from thegeneticchef.com — 'Thin Crispy Chocolate Chip Cookies - No Mixer'

Thin, crispy chocolate chip cookies with golden, rippled edges and chewy centers, buttery with a caramel flavor and loaded with chocolate chips. No mixer required — the ripples form naturally in the oven, no pan-banging. Makes about 17 cookies with a 3-tablespoon scoop.

Ingredients

  • ¾ cup (170 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
  • ¾ cup (158 g) brown sugar
  • ¼ cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • 1 cup (146 g) plus 2 tablespoons flour
  • ½ teaspoon baking soda
  • ¾ teaspoon fine salt
  • 1½ cups chocolate chips
  • Maldon salt, optional, for sprinkling on top

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 375°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
  2. Whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt together in a bowl.
  3. In a large bowl, whisk the melted butter with the brown and granulated sugars until smooth and lightened in color.
  4. Add the egg and vanilla and whisk until combined, about 30 seconds.
  5. Switch to a spatula, add the dry ingredients, and mix until just combined. Fold in the chocolate chips.
  6. Using a 3-tablespoon scoop, scoop the dough onto the prepared sheets — about 6 per sheet, spaced at least 2 inches apart to allow for spreading.
  7. Bake 9–11 minutes until the edges are golden and rippled and the centers are slightly puffed. Overbaking makes them hard and crispy.
  8. Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a cooling rack. Let the baking sheet cool before scooping the next batch.
  9. Optional: sprinkle each cookie with Maldon salt right out of the oven.

The trick to the ripples without pan-banging is more butter and less flour than a classic cookie. The cookies need the full 5-minute rest on the sheet before moving or they'll bend and break.

Velvet Vanilla Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting

Transcribed from reel

Vanilla Cake

  • 2 1/2 cups all purpose flour (325g)
  • 1 2/3 cups granulated sugar (330g)
  • 3/4 tsp baking soda
  • 3/4 tsp baking powder
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter (113g)
  • 1/3 cup vegetable oil (75g)
  • 3/4 cup water (180g)
  • 120g white chocolate (a little over 4 oz, or about 1/2 cup white chocolate chips)
  • 1/2 cup whole milk (120g)
  • 1 tbsp white vinegar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 tbsp vanilla bean paste

Cream Cheese Frosting

  • 16 oz cream cheese, room temperature (2 8 oz blocks, 453g)
  • 1 cup unsalted butter, room temperature (2 sticks, 226g)
  • 2 tsp vanilla bean paste
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 3 cups powdered sugar, sifted (360g)

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 325F (conventional, no fan) and line three 8-inch cake pans with parchment, greasing them with oil or butter.
  2. Sift the flour into a large bowl, add the sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt, and whisk until thoroughly combined and lump-free.
  3. In a saucepan over medium-low heat, stir the butter, oil, water, and white chocolate (chopped or chips) until the butter and chocolate melt; once it starts to simmer, cook and stir for one more minute.
  4. Pour the hot mixture over the dry ingredients and whisk gently just until combined with no flour streaks; do not overmix.
  5. In a glass, stir the milk and vinegar together, then add to the batter with the eggs and vanilla bean paste; fold gently until just combined into a smooth batter.
  6. Divide the batter evenly among the three pans (a scale helps); tap each pan firmly on the counter 3-5 times to release large air bubbles.
  7. Bake 18-20 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out with light, moist crumbs (no wet batter, not fully clean either).
  8. Cool the cakes in their pans for 10 minutes, then turn them out onto wire racks to cool completely.
  9. For the frosting: beat the room-temperature butter, cream cheese, vanilla bean paste, salt, and sifted powdered sugar in a stand mixer with the paddle attachment on medium speed for 2-3 minutes until smooth, fluffy, and spreadable, scraping the bowl halfway through; do not overmix or it can turn runny.
  10. If the frosting is too soft, refrigerate it for a few minutes until spreadable.
  11. Trim the domes off each cooled layer to level them (some small holes from the soda-vinegar reaction are normal).
  12. Place the first layer on a cake stand, spread with a generous amount of frosting, and repeat with all three layers.
  13. Apply a thin crumb coat over the whole cake and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
  14. Finish with the remaining frosting, decorate as desired, and serve.

  4. For the buttercream: beat the butter, powdered sugar, vanilla, salt, and a splash of heavy cream until fluffy.
  5. For the mini cookies: mix the melted butter, brown sugar, sugar, egg, and vanilla; fold in the flour, baking soda, salt, and chocolate chips.
  6. Scoop the mini cookie dough and bake at 350F for 9-11 minutes.

The Best Single Serve Chocolate Chip Cookie

Transcribed from reel

Cookie

  • 2 tbsp (26g) melted butter, cooled slightly
  • 2 tbsp (26g) light brown sugar
  • 1 tbsp (13g) white sugar
  • Splash of vanilla extract or vanilla paste
  • 1 tbsp (15g) of milk
  • 1/3 cup (40g) all purpose flour
  • 1/4 tsp salt
  • 1/4 tsp baking soda
  • 2 to 3 tbsp chocolate wafers or chopped chocolate, adjust ratio to taste
  • Sprinkle of flaky sea salt

Notes

  • If you only have dark brown sugar, use 1 tbsp of dark brown sugar with 2 tbsp of white sugar.

Steps

  1. Combine the melted and slightly cooled butter with the light brown sugar and white sugar, and whisk together.
  2. Whisk in the vanilla extract or vanilla paste.
  3. Slowly pour in the milk, whisking until the mixture is very homogenous, glossy and shiny.
  4. Separately, whisk together the flour, salt, and baking soda.
  5. Add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture and mix gently until JUST barely combined — over mixing the dough will result in a tough cookie.
  6. Fold in the chocolate wafers or chopped chocolate, as much or as little as you like.
  7. Scoop into 2 dough balls (or 1 giant cookie if you want!) and let the dough sit in the fridge for at least ~1 hour to firm up (or overnight) so the flavors marinate before baking.
  8. Right before baking, break off a few extra chocolate chunks (bittersweet or dark chocolate works best) and press them onto the top so you get a nice puddle of chocolate once baked.
  9. Bake in a preheated oven at 350°F until golden and set on the edges but still soft in the middle — 12 to 14 minutes. Check a few minutes early since every oven is different and timing depends on the size of your cookie.
  10. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt right when it comes out; it ties all the flavors together.

Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies

Transcribed from creator's website (scientificallysweet.com)

Chewy cookies with crisp edges and deep nutty brown-butter flavor; makes 14 cookies.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups (215 g) all-purpose flour
  • 3/4 tsp baking soda
  • 1/4 tsp salt (1/2 tsp if using unsalted butter)

Ingredients

  • 10 tbsp (140 g) salted butter, browned and cooled
  • 2/3 cup (145 g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1/3 cup (65 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg, room temperature
  • 1 tbsp (15 ml) milk
  • 1 tsp (5 ml) pure vanilla extract

Ingredients

  • 3 oz (85 g) dark chocolate, coarsely chopped into chunks, plus extra for topping
  • 1/2 cup (85 g) semisweet chocolate chips
  • Flaky sea salt (optional, for topping)

Steps

  1. Brown the butter: melt it in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly. It will foam and then form brown specks with a nutty aroma (8-10 minutes). Pour into a large bowl and cool to just warmer than room temperature.
  2. Whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl.
  3. Mix the cooled brown butter with both sugars in a large bowl until it looks like thick wet sand.
  4. Add the egg, milk, and vanilla; mix until well incorporated and creamy. Do not beat vigorously.
  5. Fold in the flour mixture just until mostly combined, then add the chocolate chunks and chips and mix until evenly distributed.
  6. Cover and refrigerate the dough 1-4 hours (at least 1 hour).
  7. Portion into 14 balls (about 2 oz/56 g each), roll smooth, and place 3 inches apart on prepared baking sheets. Do not flatten; press extra chocolate chunks on top if desired.
  8. Bake at 375 F (8-10 minutes) until golden on top, browned around the edges, and soft in the middle.
  9. Cool on the baking sheet 2 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. Top with flaky sea salt if desired.

For thicker cookies use 1/2 tsp baking soda. Dough balls can be frozen up to 3 months; add 1-2 minutes when baking from frozen. Cookies keep up to 3 days in an airtight container.

Chicken Chukauni

A creamy yogurt-based chicken dish: pan-fried spiced chicken tossed with onions and finished with a mustard-oil tadka swirled through whisked curd. Serve with rotis or rice.

For the Chicken

  • 400g boneless chicken (thigh recommended), cut into small cubes
  • 2 tsp ginger-garlic paste
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp pepper
  • 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder (or paprika)
  • 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
  • 1 tsp lemon juice
  • Light brush or spray of oil for frying

For the Mix

  • 1 small onion, thinly sliced (red best)
  • 1-2 green chilies, chopped
  • 3 tbsp fresh coriander leaves, chopped (divided)

For the Yogurt Base

  • 1 cup Greek yogurt
  • 1 tsp garlic paste
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp sugar

For the Tadka

  • 1.5 tbsp mustard oil (or any neutral oil)
  • 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
  • 1 tsp paprika powder
  • 1/2 tsp mustard seeds
  • 1/2 tsp fenugreek seeds (optional)

Steps

  1. Mix the chicken with ginger-garlic paste, salt, pepper, Kashmiri chili powder, turmeric and lemon juice. Rest 10-15 minutes.
  2. Brush or spray a pan with very little oil and pan-fry the chicken on medium-high until golden brown. Transfer to a bowl.
  3. Add the sliced onion, chopped chilies and half the coriander to the chicken and mix well; set aside.
  4. In another bowl, whisk the thick curd with garlic paste, salt and sugar until smooth and creamy.
  5. Heat the mustard oil until smoking hot. Turn off the heat and add the mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, turmeric and paprika.
  6. Pour the hot tadka into the curd and swirl gently to keep the streaks.
  7. Pour the yogurt mixture over the chicken mixture, mix gently, and finish with more chopped coriander leaves.
  8. Enjoy with rotis or rice.

Heat the mustard oil until it smokes to mellow its pungency before adding the spices.

Troy's World Famous Lasagna

Transcribed from reel

A meaty, cheesy lasagna with a ricotta mixture and a blended-sauce top layer finished with fresh mozzarella.

Meat Sauce

  • 1 lb ground beef
  • 1 lb ground Italian sausage (mild or hot)
  • 1 large sweet onion, chopped
  • Garlic, chopped or minced
  • About 45 oz tomato sauce (1.5 jars, or homemade)
  • Salt and pepper
  • Italian seasoning

Ricotta Mixture

  • 32 oz ricotta
  • 1 egg
  • Big handful of fresh parsley, chopped
  • Shredded mozzarella
  • Shredded or grated Parmesan
  • Salt and pepper

Assembly

  • Lasagna noodles of your choice (oven-ready are easiest)
  • Fresh mozzarella, sliced
  • Fresh parsley and basil leaves

Steps

  1. Chop the onion, parsley and garlic (if using fresh).
  2. Add oil to a pan over medium heat and saute the onions until translucent (5-7 min). Add the garlic and mix for 1 min until fragrant.
  3. Add the beef and sausage; cook together, seasoning with salt.
  4. Once cooked, remove excess grease, then add the tomato sauce and season with Italian seasoning. Simmer about 10 min to bring the flavors together.
  5. While simmering, make the ricotta mixture: combine 32 oz ricotta, 1 egg, a big handful of parsley, shredded mozzarella and shredded Parmesan; season with salt and pepper.
  6. Build the lasagna: thin layer of meat sauce on the bottom of the pan, then noodles, ricotta mixture, a sprinkle of mozzarella and Parmesan, then meat sauce. Repeat until the final layer.
  7. For the top, mix the remaining meat sauce, ricotta mixture and some shredded cheese together; top with fresh slices of mozzarella, remaining fresh parsley and fresh basil leaves.
  8. Bake at 400F for 20-40 min (depending on pan depth) until bubbling and the cheese is melted.
  9. Remove from the oven and let sit 10-15 min to set and cool before serving.

Chewy Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies

https://dumpedlingss.substack.com/p/science-based-chewy-brown-butter

Science-tested chewy brown butter chocolate chip cookies: crisp caramelised edges, a soft bendy centre, deep toffee flavour from browned butter and an overnight rest.

Ingredients (partial — full card on the linked Substack)

  • 225g unsalted butter
  • 30g ice cubes
  • 200g light brown soft sugar
  • 70g caster sugar
  • 40g golden syrup
  • 1 large egg (75–80g)
  • Strong bread flour (swapped for a third of the plain flour)
  • Dark chocolate bars, chopped (not chips)

Steps

  1. Brown the butter until it smells nutty, then add the ice cubes back in so there is enough liquid to properly dissolve the sugars.
  2. Whisk the sugars into the butter in rounds with little rests in between, taking the time to dissolve them fully.
  3. Mix in the egg, golden syrup and flours (with a third of the flour as strong bread flour for chew), then fold through the chopped dark chocolate.
  4. Rest the dough in the fridge for a full 24 hours — it bakes thicker, darker and chewier, and the flavour deepens.
  5. Roll into tall 60g balls (weigh them: every extra 10g adds nearly two minutes of bake time) and bake straight from the fridge.
  6. Pull the cookies while the middles still look underdone — 82°C internal on a probe thermometer gives a soft but not gooey centre.

The creator's full measured recipe card lives on the linked Substack; the page's recipe card did not render in full, so the ingredient list above is partial. Start the dough the day before baking.

Vanilla Whip Ganache

Transcribed from reel caption

A stable, pipeable white-chocolate vanilla ganache for cakes and desserts — made ahead and whipped to order.

Ingredients

  • 1 L heavy cream — Cream 1
  • 900 g white chocolate
  • 6 gelatin sheets
  • Vanilla paste — as needed
  • 1 L heavy cream — Cream 2 (cold)

Steps

  1. Bloom the gelatin: soak the sheets in cold water until soft.
  2. Add Cream 1 and the vanilla paste to a saucepan and heat until the cream is just about to boil.
  3. Pour the hot cream over the white chocolate. Add the squeezed-out gelatin and mix well until everything is melted and combined.
  4. Blend until completely smooth and emulsified.
  5. Add the cold Cream 2 and blend again until well combined.
  6. Pour into a clean container, cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 8 hours — overnight is best for a stable whip.
  7. The next day, whip only the amount you need until you reach the desired consistency.

Always keep the ganache cold before whipping for better volume and a more stable texture. Keep the remainder refrigerated and use as needed.

Slow Cooker Honey Sesame Chicken

https://theeverydaycookbook.com/slow-cooker-honey-sesame-chicken/

Crockpot-season dinner: chicken cooks low and slow in a sweet-savoury soy, honey and gochujang sauce, then gets shredded with broccoli and tossed with ramen noodles.

Chicken & Sauce

  • 1.5–2 lb boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs
  • ½ cup low sodium soy sauce
  • ½ cup honey
  • 1 tablespoon gochujang
  • 1 teaspoon sesame oil
  • ¼ cup ketchup
  • 1 shallot, finely diced
  • ½ yellow onion, diced
  • 1 teaspoon onion powder
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 tablespoon ginger paste
  • 1–2 tablespoons minced garlic
  • ½ teaspoon crushed red pepper
  • Salt and pepper to taste

Finish & Serve

  • 2 tablespoons cornstarch + 2 tablespoons cold water (slurry)
  • Diced broccoli (fresh or frozen)
  • 2–3 packs ramen noodles
  • Sesame seeds and sliced green onion, for garnish

Steps

  1. Add the chicken to the bottom of the slow cooker.
  2. Add the diced onion, shallot and minced garlic.
  3. Add the soy sauce, honey, gochujang, ketchup, sesame oil and all the seasonings; stir to combine.
  4. Cover and cook on low for 3–4 hours or on high for 2–3 hours.
  5. Remove the chicken and shred it with two forks.
  6. Stir the cornstarch slurry into the sauce in the slow cooker until smooth.
  7. Return the shredded chicken and add the broccoli; cook 30 minutes more (up to 1 hour for frozen broccoli).
  8. Boil the ramen noodles according to the package directions and drain.
  9. Add the noodles to the slow cooker, switch to warm, and toss until every noodle is evenly coated.
  10. Top with sesame seeds and green onions and serve immediately.

Chicken thighs give a juicier result and are more forgiving if they cook a little long. Add the noodles right before serving so they don't go soft. Store the chicken/sauce and any leftover noodles separately.

Mangalorean Prawns Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa

Transcribed from reel caption

Spicy, tangy prawns coated in a glossy ghee-roast masala, served with soft, lacy neer dosa to soak it all up — a little taste of coastal Karnataka.

Marinated Prawns

  • 500g cleaned prawns
  • ½ tsp turmeric
  • ½ tsp salt
  • 1 tsp lemon juice

Ghee Roast Masala

  • 10–12 Byadgi chillies, soaked in hot water for 15 mins
  • 1 tsp cumin
  • 2 tsp coriander seeds
  • ½ tsp fenugreek
  • ½ tsp saunf/fennel
  • 1 tsp peppercorns
  • 5–6 garlic cloves
  • Small piece ginger
  • 1 inch tamarind
  • 1 tsp jaggery (optional)
  • 6–8 cashews, soaked in water for 15–20 mins
  • Salt

Neer Dosa

  • 2 cups raw rice
  • Water
  • Salt

Steps

  1. Marinate the prawns with turmeric, salt and lemon juice for 15–20 minutes.
  2. Dry roast the spices, then grind them with the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, tamarind, cashews, jaggery and salt into a smooth paste.
  3. Heat 2 tbsp ghee and cook the prawns until just done; remove from the pan.
  4. Add 2–3 tbsp more ghee to the same pan, add the masala and cook on low-medium until glossy and aromatic.
  5. Add the prawns back and toss for 2–3 minutes.
  6. Top with a handful of curry leaves and finish with a generous drizzle of ghee.
  7. For the neer dosa: soak the rice for 4–5 hours, grind into a very smooth batter and add enough water to make it very thin, almost like buttermilk, plus salt.
  8. Pour onto a hot, lightly greased tawa, swirl, cover and cook until set — no flipping needed. Serve hot.

No-Bake French Silk Pudding

https://www.cake-babe.com/no-bake-french-silk-pudding/

French silk pie flavour without the work: silky chocolate pudding layered with Oreo Thins that soften overnight into cake-like layers, topped with whipped cream. No oven required.

Chocolate Pudding

  • 1 box (3.4 oz) instant chocolate pudding mix
  • 1¼ cups cold milk
  • 1 can (13.4 oz) sweetened condensed milk
  • 2 packages Oreo Thins (reserve 4–5, crushed, for topping)
  • 2 cups heavy cream
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Topping

  • 1 cup heavy whipping cream
  • 1 tablespoon powdered sugar

Steps

  1. In a large bowl, whisk together the cold milk and sweetened condensed milk. Sprinkle the pudding mix over the top and whisk by hand for 2–3 minutes until smooth. Chill 10 minutes to thicken.
  2. While the pudding sets, beat the 2 cups heavy cream with the vanilla until stiff peaks form.
  3. With a rubber spatula, gently fold the whipped cream into the pudding until no streaks remain.
  4. Spread a thin layer of pudding in your dish, cups or trifle bowl, then add a neat layer of whole Oreo Thins. Repeat for 2–3 layers.
  5. Finish with a final layer of pudding that fully covers everything, sealing the edges so the cookies stay soft.
  6. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 6 hours and up to 24 hours.
  7. Right before serving, beat the topping cream with the powdered sugar to medium peaks, spread over the pudding and sprinkle with the reserved crushed Oreos.

Use instant pudding mix, not cook-and-serve. Serves 12; best within 24 hours of assembling.

One-Pan, Speedy Thai Peanut Chickpea Curry (Curry in a Hurry)

https://boldbeanco.com/blogs/beanspo-recipes/store-cupboard-thai-chickpea-curry

Zena Kamgaing's satay-ish chickpea curry from her 'Dinner Time' cookbook, shared on the Bold Bean Co. website — a 15-minute, one-pan Thai peanut curry built on store-cupboard ingredients.

Ingredients

  • 1 jar Queen Chickpeas — with their bean stock
  • 2 x 400g tins of good-quality coconut milk (70% or more coconut extract)
  • 100g smooth natural peanut butter
  • 1 tbsp good-quality Thai red curry paste
  • 1 tbsp mild curry powder
  • 1 tbsp light soy sauce
  • 1 tsp sugar
  • 200ml boiling water
  • 200g baby spinach
  • ½ lime, juice
  • To serve: cooked rice and/or warmed flatbreads; roasted peanuts, finely chopped (optional)

Steps

  1. Place the chickpeas, coconut milk, peanut butter, curry paste, curry powder, soy sauce and sugar in a medium saucepan and set it over a high heat.
  2. Stir in the boiling water and bring the liquid to a simmer, stirring frequently to prevent the curry sauce sticking. Reduce the heat to medium-high and cook, again stirring frequently, for 5 minutes.
  3. Add the baby spinach and lime juice, stirring until the spinach has wilted, then season with salt and pepper.
  4. Serve the curry in bowls with rice and/or flatbreads, and if you want some crunch, scatter over a few roasted peanuts.

Feeds 2–3.

Jhol Maggi (Kathmandu-Inspired)

Nepali-style jhol Maggi — instant noodles in a spicy, brothy, slurpy soup with mustard oil, tangy tomatoes, green chillies and citrusy Timur. Comfort food from the hills.

Ingredients

  • 1 packet Maggi + tastemaker
  • 1 tbsp mustard oil
  • 4–5 garlic cloves, finely chopped
  • 1 small onion, sliced
  • 1 green chilli, chopped/slit
  • 2 medium tomatoes, chopped
  • 1/2 tsp red chilli powder
  • 1/4 tsp turmeric
  • 1/4 tsp crushed Timur (Nepali Sichuan pepper)
  • Salt, as required
  • 1 3/4–2 cups water
  • Fresh coriander
  • 1/2 lemon
  • Chilli oil/crisp, optional

Steps

  1. Heat the mustard oil until lightly smoking. Add the garlic, onion and green chilli and sauté until aromatic.
  2. Add the tomatoes, chilli powder, turmeric, Timur and a little salt. Cook until the tomatoes completely soften and turn jammy.
  3. Add 1 3/4–2 cups water and simmer for 5–7 minutes to build a flavourful, tangy broth.
  4. Add the Maggi tastemaker and noodles and cook until the noodles are done, keeping plenty of jhol/broth in the pan.
  5. Finish with fresh coriander, a squeeze of lemon and some chilli crisp on top if you like it extra spicy.

Transcribed from the creator's own comment on the reel. No Timur? Use freshly crushed black pepper + a little lemon zest for that peppery, citrusy kick. Serve piping hot.

Jacques Torres Chocolate Chip Cookies

https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015819-chocolate-chip-cookies

A cookie-tasting series entry testing the famous Jacques Torres recipe (David Leite adaptation from NYT Cooking): tall, chewy cookies with big chocolate disks, aged dough, and a sprinkle of sea salt. Makes 18 large (3.5 oz) cookies.

Ingredients

    Steps

    1. Sift flours, baking soda, baking powder and salt into a bowl. Set aside.
    2. Using a mixer fitted with paddle attachment, cream butter and sugars together until very light, about 5 minutes. Add eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Stir in the vanilla. Reduce speed to low, add dry ingredients and mix until just combined, 5 to 10 seconds. Drop chocolate pieces in and incorporate them without breaking them. Press plastic wrap against dough and refrigerate for 24 to 36 hours. Dough may be used in batches, and can be refrigerated for up to 72 hours.
    3. When ready to bake, preheat oven to 350 degrees. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a nonstick baking mat. Set aside.
    4. Scoop 6 3 1/2-ounce mounds of dough (the size of generous golf balls) onto baking sheet, making sure to turn horizontally any chocolate pieces that are poking up; it will make for a more attractive cookie. Sprinkle lightly with salt and bake until golden brown but still soft, 18 to 20 minutes. Transfer sheet to a wire rack for 10 minutes, then slip cookies onto another rack to cool a bit more. Repeat with remaining dough, or reserve dough, refrigerated, for baking remaining batches the next day. Eat warm, with a big napkin.

        Goan Meatballs in Tomato Curry

        https://niksharmacooks.com/goan-meatballs-in-tomato-curry/

        Juicy baked beef-and-chorizo meatballs in a tangy tomato curry with curry leaves, Kashmiri chile and tamarind - inspired by Nik Sharma's grandmother Lucy, with a baking-soda trick that raises the meat's pH so the proteins hold onto more water. Serve over rice or with flatbread; also good in pasta or sandwiches.

        Ingredients

          Ingredients

            Steps

            1. To make the meatballs, place the ground beef in a large mixing bowl, sprinkle with the baking soda and 2 Tbsp water, and mix. Cover and let sit for 15 minutes.
            2. Preheat the oven to 400F [200C]. Spray or brush a baking sheet with oil.
            3. Add the chorizo, shallot, panko, egg yolk, garlic, green chilli, cilantro, mint, ginger, salt, and turmeric to the ground beef and combine. Roll the meat into 2 Tbsp balls, using a cookie scoop or measuring spoon, and place them on the prepared baking sheet. You can also wet your hands with water when shaping the meatballs, which will prevent the meat from sticking to your hands. You should get approximately 25 meatballs. Roast until the meatballs are golden brown and caramelized, 6 to 8 minutes. Cut a meatball; the inside should be completely opaque, and the internal temperature should reach 160F [71C]. Remove from the oven.
            4. While the meatballs cook, to make the curry, in a medium Dutch oven or saucepan over medium-high heat, melt the ghee. Add the curry leaves, shallot, and a pinch of salt, turn the heat to medium-low, and saute until fragrant, translucent, and soft, 4 to 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, Kashmiri chilli powder, coriander, turmeric, black pepper, and cumin and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add 7 oz [200 g] of the crushed tomatoes and reserve the rest for another purpose. Stir in 1 cup [240 ml] water and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then turn the heat to low and simmer. Stir in the tamarind paste and season with salt. Add the meatballs, gently toss to coat in the sauce, and let simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat. Garnish with the cilantro and serve hot or warm with rice or flatbread.
            5. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.

            Creamy Vodka Orzo with Rotisserie Chicken

            A creamy one-pot-ish orzo in vodka-spiked tomato sauce with parmesan and shredded rotisserie chicken - 'refuse to spend money at restaurants when food at home is this good'.

            Ingredients

              Steps

              1. Finely dice the shallot and crush/mince the garlic.
              2. Saute both in olive oil over medium-low heat until softened.
              3. Season with black pepper, then add the tomato paste and cook it down.
              4. Add an optional splash of vodka - it blooms in the oil for flavor.
              5. Stir in the dry orzo, then add the broth (about a 1 to 2 ratio of orzo to liquid) and let it simmer until the pasta absorbs the liquid and thickens.
              6. While it cooks, grate a large amount of Parmesan and shred the rotisserie chicken.
              7. Stir in the heavy cream, Parmesan, and shredded chicken. Top with extra cheese and serve.

                                    Jalapeño Popper Chicken Cheddar Bay Biscuit Soup

                                    Transcribed from theeverydaycookbook.com (the creator's linked recipe page)

                                    This jalapeño popper chicken soup combines cream cheese, shredded cheddar, bacon, and jalapeños in a creamy chicken broth and tops individual bowls with Red Lobster Cheddar Bay biscuit dough baked until golden for an easy impressive dinner.

                                    Ingredients

                                      Ingredients

                                        Ingredients

                                          Steps

                                          1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (for the biscuit topping).
                                          2. In a Dutch oven or large pot, melt the butter over medium heat.
                                          3. Add the diced onion and diced jalapeños and cook until softened and the onions are translucent. Add the minced garlic and mix until well combined.
                                          4. Slowly add the flour in small increments, stirring constantly, until a roux forms.
                                          5. Pour in the chicken stock or bone broth and add the crushed red pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper.
                                          6. Add the cooked chicken and bacon bits; stir and bring to a gentle simmer.
                                          7. After simmering 5-10 minutes, whisk in the softened cream cheese until completely smooth with no clumps.
                                          8. Reduce the heat to low and add the shredded cheddar and half and half. Stir until melted and creamy.
                                          9. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, then taste and season with salt and pepper. (If skipping the biscuit topping, serve now garnished with bacon, cheese, green onion, or sour cream.)
                                          10. Prepare the biscuit dough according to the box directions, with the extra cheddar folded in.
                                          11. Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls without overfilling, then gently drop 1-2 tablespoons of biscuit dough onto the top of each bowl.
                                          12. Bake uncovered for 14-16 minutes, until the dough is golden brown.
                                          13. Remove from the oven and immediately brush the hot biscuits with the garlic butter seasoning from the biscuit mix. Garnish with green onions and serve right away.

                                          Any fully cooked chicken works in place of rotisserie (baked or poached breasts shredded by hand are equally good). Instead of individual bowls, the biscuit dough can be scooped onto the soup in an oven-safe Dutch oven and baked uncovered the same way. Store soup and unbaked biscuit dough separately — the soup keeps in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days; reheat on the stovetop over medium-low heat or in the microwave, adding a splash of broth if it thickened.

                                          Crispy Panko Chicken Tenders with Fresh Tomato Sauce

                                          Transcribed from reel

                                          The creator's go-to company dinner: crispy panko-crusted chicken tenders with a garden tomato sauce that cooks down in 30 minutes — impressive-looking and ready in half an hour.

                                          Ingredients

                                            Ingredients

                                              Steps

                                              1. Sauce: add the tomatoes, olive oil, salt, basil, garlic, onion, and a splash of water or stock to a pot.
                                              2. Cook down for about 30 minutes, until the tomato skins have broken down and their juices have released.
                                              3. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth; taste and add salt until it's just right.
                                              4. Chicken: slice each chicken breast in half, then quarter to make 4 tenders (leave larger if preferred). Pound thin between two sheets of plastic wrap.
                                              5. Coat each tender in flour, then beaten egg, then seasoned panko; repeat until all are coated.
                                              6. Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a frying pan over medium heat; once smoking, add 2-3 cutlets and cook 3-4 minutes per side, until the panko is golden brown and the edges visibly crispy.
                                              7. Rest on a wire rack or paper towels to crisp up.
                                              8. Serve with pasta or spaghetti squash, topped with the tomato sauce, fresh grated parmesan, and chopped basil.

                                              The creator notes that sauce is 'not an exact science — measure with your heart and taste and add salt until it's just right.' The batch in the reel made far more than 2 cups of sauce because of a large tomato harvest.

                                              Butter Chicken Bunny Chow

                                              Transcribed from reel

                                              Chicken & Marinade

                                              • 4 chicken fillets, cubed
                                              • 4 thigh fillets, cubed
                                              • 6 tbsp plain yoghurt
                                              • 3 tsp ginger garlic
                                              • ½ lemon, juiced
                                              • 1½ tsp crushed cumin
                                              • 1½ tsp crushed coriander seeds
                                              • ½ tsp turmeric
                                              • 1 tsp chilli powder
                                              • 1½ tsp salt
                                              • ½ tsp black pepper

                                              Sauce

                                              • 1 tbsp ghee
                                              • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
                                              • 1½ tsp ginger garlic
                                              • 1 tsp coriander powder
                                              • 1 tsp garam masala
                                              • ½ tsp turmeric
                                              • 1 tsp chilli powder
                                              • 50 g tomato paste
                                              • 40 g butter
                                              • Cream, to finish

                                              Soft White Loaf (bunny chow bread)

                                              • 4 cups cake flour
                                              • 7 g instant yeast
                                              • 2½ tsp sugar
                                              • 1¼ tsp salt
                                              • ⅓ cup oil
                                              • ¾ cup lukewarm milk
                                              • ¾ cup lukewarm water

                                              Steps

                                              1. Add the chicken to a bowl with the yoghurt, ginger garlic, lemon juice, cumin, crushed coriander seeds, turmeric, chilli powder, salt and pepper. Mix well, cover and marinate for a few hours.
                                              2. Heat a heavy pot over medium-high heat and add the marinated chicken. Cook until nicely browned and almost cooked through. Remove and set aside.
                                              3. In the same pan, add the ghee and onion; cook until softened and lightly golden.
                                              4. Add the ginger garlic, coriander powder, garam masala, turmeric and chilli powder; cook briefly until fragrant.
                                              5. Add the tomato paste and butter; cook down a few minutes until the tomato paste darkens slightly and the butter begins to separate.
                                              6. Return the chicken to the pan and mix well so it's coated in sauce. Simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens.
                                              7. Finish with a generous splash of cream, stir through, taste and adjust seasoning. Top with coriander and serve.

                                              Mix, knead and proof the dough, bake into a loaf, hollow out and fill with the butter chicken.

                                              Chicken & Chickpea Kebabs

                                              Transcribed from reel

                                              Protein-packed and healthy if air-fried.

                                              Ingredients

                                              • 2 cups soaked chickpeas (1 cup raw chickpeas soaked overnight)
                                              • 1 chicken breast
                                              • 1 potato
                                              • 2 onions
                                              • 1 tbsp coriander seeds
                                              • 1 tsp cumin seeds
                                              • 10–15 black peppercorns
                                              • 4 dried red chillies
                                              • 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
                                              • 1 tsp turmeric powder
                                              • 1 tsp garam masala powder
                                              • Salt
                                              • ½ cup water

                                              Steps

                                              1. In a pressure cooker add the soaked chickpeas, chicken breast, potato, onions, the whole spices, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, garam masala, salt and ½ cup water. Cook until done.
                                              2. Open the lid and remove the chicken breast; shred it.
                                              3. For the chickpea mixture, switch on the flame and dry the mixture completely, mashing with a masher for a smooth texture. Add 1–2 tbsp ghee.
                                              4. Add the shredded chicken and mix well.
                                              5. Transfer to a bowl and let cool. Then add 1 egg, coriander leaves, 2–3 green chillies and 1 tbsp lemon juice.
                                              6. Mix well, shape into kebabs and fry in hot oil (or air-fry for a healthier version).

                                              Christina calls this her secret weapon for every holiday and birthday — she's been making it year-round for almost five years. An Oreo cookie crust, a rich and silky chocolate custard 'pudding' filling, and a fluffy vanilla bean whipped cream on top.

                                              Ingredients

                                                Ingredients

                                                  Ingredients

                                                    Steps

                                                    1. Heat your oven to 350 degrees.
                                                    2. Put Oreos in a food processor and pulse until the texture of sand. Add in the butter and pulse again until combined. Transfer to a pie dish and press the Oreos onto the surface of the dish until an even crust is formed. Place in the oven for 15 minutes, then let cool.
                                                    3. Whisk together the egg yolks, half & half and cream in a large bowl; set aside.
                                                    4. Add the sugar, cocoa powder, salt and corn starch to a tall-sided pan. Whisk together. Turn to medium-low heat and add in the liquid egg mixture. Whisk to combine. Stir continuously until the mixture comes to a soft boil and becomes thick — this should take about 10 minutes and be thick like a soft pudding.
                                                    5. Remove from the heat and add in the chocolate and vanilla extract. Stir until melted. Add in the butter and mix.
                                                    6. Pour the filling into the pie crust and cover with plastic wrap, letting the plastic wrap sit directly on top of the filling (this stops condensation forming in the fridge). Chill in the fridge for at least 8 hours or overnight.
                                                    7. For the whipped cream: combine the cold heavy cream, sugar and vanilla in a mixer. Beat with a whisk attachment until whipped cream forms (a couple of minutes). Serve on top of the pie, add some chocolate shavings and enjoy.

                                                        Street Style Bun Kabab

                                                        Transcribed from reel caption

                                                        Pakistani street-style bun kabab: spiced potato-and-daal kababs fried in egg, tucked into butter-toasted buns with green chutney, onion rings and ketchup.

                                                        Kabab

                                                        • 3 potatoes
                                                        • 1 cup daal channa
                                                        • 1 tablespoon freshly minced garlic
                                                        • Salt
                                                        • 1 tablespoon all spice powder
                                                        • ½ teaspoon amchoor powder
                                                        • 3–4 red round peppers
                                                        • 3–4 cloves
                                                        • 7–8 black peppercorns
                                                        • ½ teaspoon chilli flakes
                                                        • 1 teaspoon coriander powder
                                                        • 1 tablespoon pomegranate powder
                                                        • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
                                                        • 1.5 litres water
                                                        • Coriander leaves
                                                        • Chaat masala, to finish

                                                        Green Chutney

                                                        • Mint leaves
                                                        • Coriander leaves
                                                        • Green chillies
                                                        • Lemon juice
                                                        • Salt
                                                        • Roasted crushed cumin
                                                        • Yogurt

                                                        Assembly

                                                        • Buns, butter-toasted
                                                        • Whisked eggs, to coat the kababs
                                                        • Onion rings
                                                        • Ketchup

                                                        Steps

                                                        1. Boil the potatoes and daal channa with all the kabab spices in 1.5 litres of water until completely cooked. (Don't use pre-boiled potatoes or daal — boiling them with the spices builds the flavour.)
                                                        2. Strain off the excess water; remove the cloves and peppercorns; mash everything with a masher or fork.
                                                        3. Mix in the lemon juice and chaat masala, let the mixture cool, then shape into kababs.
                                                        4. Dip the kababs in whisked egg and shallow-fry until golden (anda-style).
                                                        5. Blend the green chutney ingredients until smooth.
                                                        6. Toast the buns with butter and assemble with a fried kabab, green chutney, onion rings and ketchup.

                                                        Use freshly made all-spice powder and freshly grated garlic for the best flavour, and don't skip the green chutney. Soak the onion rings in iced water and drizzle with lemon before serving.
